title: Blob Storage Basics
description: Understand Azure Blob Storage concepts including block blobs, append blobs, and page blobs for different workload patterns.

data.text: Blob Storage is Azure's object storage service for unstructured data like documents, images, videos, backups, and logs. A **blob** (binary large object) lives inside a **container**, which lives inside a storage account. Blobs are ideal when you need cheap, scalable storage with an HTTP-based API.
Azure Blob Storage offers three blob types, each designed for a different pattern. Choosing the right one affects performance, cost, and what operations you can perform.

data.title: Blob Types
items: **Block blobs** — the default and most common type. Made of blocks of data that can be uploaded independently and then committed. Perfect for files, images, and backups.
**Append blobs** — optimized for append-only operations like logs and audit trails. Each write adds to the end of the blob without rewriting existing content.
**Page blobs** — made of 512-byte pages that can be read or written individually. Used primarily for VHD files and managed disks.

data.title: Create a Container with Azure CLI
data.content: Set up a blob container for storing uploads
data.code:
az storage container create \
  --account-name stdemostorage \
  --name uploads \
  --public-access blob

data.title: Upload a Blob with Azure CLI
data.content: Upload a local file to a blob container
data.code:
az storage blob upload \
  --account-name stdemostorage \
  --container-name uploads \
  --name photo.jpg \
  --file ./photo.jpg \
  --auth-mode login

terms.definition: A logical grouping of blobs inside a storage account, similar to a folder in a file system.
A blob composed of blocks that can be uploaded separately and then committed. Ideal for most file storage scenarios.
A blob optimized for append-only writes, commonly used for logging and audit trails.
A blob made of 512-byte pages, used for VHD files and virtual machine disks.

data.title: Blob URLs
data.text: Every blob has a URL: https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<blob>. You can use this URL directly in web pages, APIs, or download managers.

data.title: Exercise: Upload and Inspect a Blob
data.description: Create a container, upload a file, and view its properties in the Azure Portal.
steps: Create a container named 'demo-images' in your storage account.
Upload any image file to the container.
Open the blob and note its URL, size, and last modified time.
Try changing the public access level and observe the URL behavior.
data.expectedOutcome: A successfully uploaded blob with a working public URL if access level allows it.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Blob Storage stores unstructured files at any scale.
Block blobs are the default choice for most scenarios.
Containers group blobs and control access levels.
You can manage blobs with Azure CLI, REST APIs, or SDKs.
data.takeaway: Blob Storage is the workhorse of Azure data storage. Next, you will learn how containers and blob metadata help you organize data.
